relevance: Widely used momentum / trend indicator.

title: Combined MACD Signal
variables: S_k = short lookback for signal k  ;  L_k = long lookback for signal k
intuition: Combine multiple MACD signals across different time scales.
relevance: Diversifies trend-signal horizons.

title: Interest Rate Differential
variables: i^A = interest rate of currency A  ;  i^B = interest rate of currency B  ;  IRD = interest rate differential
intuition: Carry is earned from the difference between currency interest rates.
relevance: Basis of FX carry strategies.

title: Carry Trade Daily Interest Earned
variables: I = interest earned per day  ;  C = notional capital  ;  l = leverage  ;  i^A, i^B = interest rates
intuition: Daily carry equals the rate spread times notional and leverage, divided by 365.
relevance: Quantifies expected carry income.

title: Equally Weighted Long-Only Vol-Targeted Portfolio
variables: r^p_t = portfolio return  ;  N_t = number of assets  ;  sigma_tgt = target volatility  ;  sigma^i_t = asset volatility  ;  r^i_{t,t+1} = asset return
intuition: Average across assets while scaling each one by its volatility.
relevance: Baseline long-only risk-controlled strategy.

title: Net Exposure
variables: V_long = dollar value of long positions  ;  V_short = dollar value of short positions  ;  V_portfolio = total capital
intuition: Measures how much net market direction the portfolio carries.
relevance: Long-short and market-neutral risk management.

title: Long-Short Portfolio Return
variables: w_L = weight of long positions  ;  w_S = weight of short positions  ;  r^L = long-basket return  ;  r^S = short-basket return
intuition: Portfolio return equals weighted long returns minus weighted short returns.
relevance: Core long-short strategy equation.

title: Deep Momentum Network Position Function
variables: w_i^t = position / weight for asset i at time t  ;  u_i^t = market features  ;  theta = neural-network parameters  ;  f = predictive network
intuition: A neural network directly outputs trading positions from market features.
relevance: End-to-end strategy learning (Deep Momentum Networks).

title: Deep Momentum Network Return Loss and Sharpe Loss
equation: L_returns = -mean R; L_sharpe = -mean R sqrt(252)/std R
variables: mu_R = average strategy return  ;  R(i,t) = strategy return for asset i at time t  ;  Omega = universe of observations, N = sample size  ;  w_i^t = model position  ;  sigma_tgt = target vol, sigma^i_t = asset vol
intuition: Train the model to maximize returns or the Sharpe ratio directly.
relevance: Direct optimization of trading objectives (not just prediction error).

title: Cross-Sectional Momentum Portfolio Return
variables: X_i^t = trading signal / position for security i  ;  N = number of assets  ;  sigma_tgt / sigma^i_t = volatility scaling  ;  r^i_{t,t+1} = future return
intuition: Average volatility-scaled returns across assets chosen by a cross-sectional signal.
relevance: Foundation of cross-sectional momentum.

title: Cross-Sectional Momentum Score Calculation
variables: Y_i^t = score for asset i  ;  u_i^t = input vector / features  ;  f = predictive model
intuition: Compute a score for every asset in the universe.
relevance: First step in ranking-based portfolio construction.

title: Cross-Sectional Momentum Score Ranking
variables: Z_i^t = rank of asset i  ;  R(.) = ranking operator  ;  Y_i^t = score
intuition: Sort assets by predicted score.
relevance: Converts model outputs into tradable ranks.

title: Cross-Sectional Momentum Security Selection
equation: X = -1 if Z<=0.1N; +1 if Z>0.9N; else 0
variables: X_i^t = position signal (+1 long / -1 short / 0 flat)  ;  Z_i^t = rank of asset i  ;  N = number of assets
intuition: Short the bottom decile, long the top decile, and ignore the middle.
relevance: Common cross-sectional momentum construction.

title: Raw Cumulative Return Score
variables: Y_i^t = asset score  ;  r^i_{t-252,t} = prior 252-day (12-month) return
intuition: Use the past 12-month return as the ranking score.
relevance: Classical momentum factor.

title: Learning-to-Rank Score Calculation
variables: Y_i^t = predicted score / target  ;  u_i^t = features  ;  theta = model parameters
intuition: Use a trained model rather than a raw momentum heuristic to score assets.
relevance: Regress-then-rank portfolio construction.

title: Volatility-Normalized MSE Loss for Score Training
variables: target_i^t = chosen target (e.g. vol-normalized future return)  ;  Y_i^t = predicted score  ;  Omega = training universe, N = sample size
intuition: Train scores to match future realized target values.
relevance: Supervised learning for cross-sectional ranking.

title: Pointwise Learning-to-Rank Loss
variables: x_i, x_j = paired assets / examples  ;  f = pairwise scoring function  ;  l = loss function  ;  y_i = target preference / label
intuition: Train the model to learn which asset should rank above another.
relevance: Learning-to-rank methods for portfolio construction.

title: HAR Model for Realized Volatility
equation: v_{d,t+1} = b0 + b1 v_d + b2 v_w + b3 v_m + eps
variables: v_{d,t+1} = next-day volatility  ;  v_{d,t} = daily volatility  ;  v_{w,t} = weekly volatility  ;  v_{m,t} = monthly volatility  ;  beta = coefficients, eps_t = error
intuition: Forecast next volatility using daily, weekly, and monthly components.
relevance: Popular realized-volatility forecasting model (Heterogeneous Autoregressive).

title: Realized Volatility Estimate
variables: RV_t = realized volatility for day t  ;  r_i^t = high-frequency return in intraday interval i  ;  m = number of intraday intervals
intuition: Estimate volatility by summing squared intraday returns.
relevance: Uses high-frequency data for sharper volatility estimation.

title: HEAVY Model
equation: v_{d,t+1} = a + b v_{d,t} + g RV_t + eps
variables: v_{d,t+1} = forecast volatility  ;  v_{d,t} = lagged volatility  ;  RV_t = realized volatility  ;  alpha, beta, gamma = model parameters  ;  eps_t = error
intuition: Add realized-volatility information to improve volatility forecasts.
relevance: Captures short-term volatility from high-frequency data (HEAVY).

title: Mean-Variance Portfolio Optimization
equation: max w^T r  s.t. w^T S w = sigma0^2, w^T 1 = 1
variables: r_p = portfolio expected return  ;  w = portfolio weights  ;  r = vector of expected asset returns  ;  Sigma = covariance matrix  ;  sigma_{p,0}^2 = target risk level, 1 = vector of ones
intuition: Maximize expected return while holding risk at a target and fully investing capital.
relevance: Classical Markowitz portfolio optimization.

title: Portfolio Variance / Risk Minimization
equation: min w^T S w  s.t. w^T r = r0, w^T 1 = 1
variables: sigma_p^2 = portfolio variance  ;  w = weights, Sigma = covariance matrix  ;  r_{p,0} = target expected return  ;  w^T 1 = 1 = full-investment constraint
intuition: Find the lowest-risk portfolio that still hits a desired return.
relevance: Portfolio construction under constraints.

title: Mean-Variance Lagrangian
equation: L = w^T S w + lam(r0 - w^T r) + gam(1 - w^T 1)
variables: lambda, gamma = Lagrange multipliers  ;  w = weights, Sigma = covariance, r = expected returns  ;  r_{p,0} = target return
intuition: Convert the constrained optimization into an unconstrained one.
relevance: Analytical route to the optimal mean-variance portfolio.

title: First-Order Conditions for Mean-Variance
equation: 2 S w - lam r - gam 1 = 0; constraints = 0
variables: Sigma = covariance matrix, w = weights  ;  lambda, gamma = Lagrange multipliers  ;  r = expected returns, 1 = ones vector
intuition: Solve for the optimal portfolio by setting all gradients to zero.
relevance: Closed-form constrained optimization conditions.

title: Diversification Ratio
variables: DR = diversification ratio  ;  w = weights  ;  sigma = vector of individual asset volatilities  ;  Sigma = covariance matrix
intuition: Compare weighted standalone risk to the actual (lower) portfolio risk.
relevance: Measures the diversification benefit of a portfolio.

title: Maximum Diversification Optimization
equation: max (w^T sigma)/sqrt(w^T S w)  s.t. w^T 1 = 1
variables: w = weights, sigma = volatility vector  ;  Sigma = covariance matrix
intuition: Choose weights that maximize the diversification ratio.
relevance: Alternative to mean-variance optimization.

title: Maximum Diversification Lagrangian
equation: L = w^T sigma - lam(w^T S w - 1) - gam(w^T 1 - 1)
variables: lambda, gamma = Lagrange multipliers  ;  w = weights, sigma = volatility vector  ;  Sigma = covariance matrix
intuition: Optimize diversification while enforcing the risk and weight constraints.
relevance: Analytical form of maximum diversification.

title: First-Order Conditions for Maximum Diversification
equation: sigma - 2 lam S w - gam 1 = 0; constraints = 0
variables: sigma = volatility vector, Sigma = covariance  ;  w = weights, lambda, gamma = multipliers
intuition: Conditions that identify the optimal maximum-diversification portfolio.
relevance: Portfolio optimization math.

title: Deep Learning Mean-Variance Portfolio Objective
variables: w_t = portfolio weights at time t  ;  r_{p,t+1} = next-period portfolio return  ;  lambda = risk aversion  ;  n = number of assets
intuition: Maximize expected return minus a variance penalty, with absolute weights summing to one.
relevance: Differentiable deep-learning portfolio optimization.

title: Neural Network Portfolio Weight Function
variables: w_t = portfolio weights  ;  X_t = network inputs (market data)  ;  f = neural network
intuition: A neural network maps market data directly into portfolio weights.
relevance: End-to-end portfolio construction.

title: Score Block / Fitness Score Network
variables: s_t = vector of asset fitness scores  ;  s_{i,t} = score for asset i  ;  f_scores = score network  ;  X_t = input data
intuition: First produce scores indicating which assets deserve larger weights.
relevance: Separates scoring from the portfolio-constraint transformation.

title: Portfolio Block Signed-Softmax Weights
variables: w_{i,t} = weight for asset i  ;  s_{i,t} = score  ;  sign(.) = long / short direction  ;  N = number of assets
intuition: Turn score signs into long/short direction and score magnitudes into allocation size.
relevance: Differentiable long-short portfolio weighting.

title: Global Minimum Variance Portfolio Objective
variables: w_t = portfolio weights  ;  r_{p,t+1} = next-period portfolio return
intuition: Find the weights that minimize portfolio variance.
relevance: Risk-first portfolio construction.

title: Maximum Sharpe Ratio Portfolio Objective
variables: E = expected return  ;  Std = standard deviation  ;  r_{p,t+1} = portfolio return
intuition: Maximize return per unit of risk.
relevance: Central portfolio performance objective.

title: Long-Only Softmax Constraint
variables: w_{i,t} = nonnegative portfolio weight  ;  s_{i,t} = score  ;  n = number of assets
intuition: Softmax converts scores into positive weights that sum to one.
relevance: Long-only differentiable portfolio construction.

title: Maximum Position Constraint (Generalized Sigmoid)
variables: u = maximum position limit  ;  a = generalized-sigmoid offset (chosen from u)  ;  phi_a = generalized sigmoid transform
intuition: Limit how large any single position can become.
relevance: Risk control through differentiable position constraints.

title: Cardinality Constraint Portfolio Construction
variables: d_u = upper score threshold  ;  d_l = lower score threshold  ;  s~_t = sorted scores  ;  k = cutoff index
intuition: Only the strongest long and short candidates receive weights.
relevance: Controls the number of active holdings (cardinality).

title: NeuralSort Sorting Matrix Construction
variables: Lambda^t = sorting score matrix  ;  s_{j,t} = score for asset j  ;  n = number of assets  ;  i = target rank index
intuition: Build a differentiable structure whose row-maxima encode a ranking.
relevance: Used for NeuralSort / differentiable sorting.

title: Permutation Matrix from Sorting Scores
variables: Pi(s_t) = permutation / sorting matrix  ;  Lambda^t_{i,:} = row i of the sorting-score matrix
intuition: Hard sorting picks the largest value in each row to form a permutation.
relevance: Ranking is needed to apply cardinality constraints.

title: Differentiable Softmax Approximation to Sorting
variables: Pihat = soft permutation matrix  ;  softmax = differentiable approximation to argmax
intuition: Replace hard sorting with a differentiable soft sort.
relevance: Allows gradient descent to flow through ranking decisions.

title: Leverage Constraint Weight Transformation
variables: L = leverage / gross-exposure factor  ;  s_{i,t} = score  ;  n = number of assets
intuition: Scale total exposure up or down while preserving the relative weights.
relevance: Implements leverage constraints in a differentiable portfolio.

title: Graph-HAR Model
equation: v_{d,t+1} = a + b v + g Ahat v  (daily/weekly/monthly)
variables: v_d, v_w, v_m = daily / weekly / monthly volatility vectors  ;  Atilde = normalized adjacency matrix  ;  beta = own-volatility coefficients  ;  gamma = neighbor / spillover coefficients
intuition: Forecast volatility using each asset's own history and its neighbors' histories.
relevance: Captures cross-asset volatility spillovers.

title: GNN-HAR Model
equation: v_{d,t+1} = a + V_t b + H^l g;  H^l = sigma(Ahat H^{l-1} W^l)
variables: V_t = volatility feature matrix  ;  H^(l) = graph neural representation  ;  A / Atilde = adjacency matrix  ;  W^(l) = trainable GNN weights
intuition: Replace linear neighbor aggregation with graph neural layers.
relevance: Models nonlinear cross-asset dependencies.

title: Graph-Based Portfolio GCN Layer
variables: H^(l) = graph node features  ;  Ahat = normalized adjacency matrix  ;  W^(l) = graph convolution weights  ;  sigma = activation
intuition: Update node / company / asset features by aggregating connected-neighbor information.
relevance: Graph-based portfolio construction.

title: Joint Prediction of Future Returns and Weights
variables: r = returns  ;  w = portfolio weights  ;  x = macroeconomic / text / feature inputs  ;  L = lookback window, H = forecast horizon  ;  f = predictive model
intuition: Use recent returns and features to forecast future returns and portfolio weights together.
relevance: Hybrid models combine time-series and contextual (e.g. LLM / macro) information.

title: Hybrid MSE plus Decision Loss
variables: L_MSE = prediction-error loss  ;  L_Decision = loss measuring suboptimal portfolio decisions  ;  beta = weighting parameter in [0, 1]
intuition: Train not only to predict accurately, but also to make better portfolio decisions.
relevance: Decision-aware machine learning for finance.
